facts.fact: The Department of Home Affairs reports that its online birth registration system was available at 242 health facilities by the end of the 2024/25 financial year, and that birth registration is performed at high-volume hospitals; the report states no digital system for registering deaths.

The Department of Home Affairs describes birth registration at health facilities as an online birth registration system, extended by improving connectivity at health centres under its Birth Optimisation Strategy; it does not describe how the record reaches the National Population Register.

The Department of Home Affairs reports 242 health facilities with access to online birth registration at the end of 2024/25, after 48 Priority 4 health facilities were added in the year; it gives no total of health facilities, and separately counts 325 frontline offices and 220 mobile units without saying how those register a birth.

The Department of Home Affairs reports that in the 2024/25 financial year (April 2024 to March 2025) the online birth registration system was rolled out in 48 Priority 4 health facilities, taking the total from 194 to 242.
The Department of Home Affairs itself rolls out the online birth registration system to health facilities and reports on it in its own annual report for 2024/25.
The Department of Home Affairs says the 2024/25 rollout of online birth registration to health facilities follows the increased footprint plan of its Birth Optimisation Strategy.
